title: Capacity Binder: enterprise throughput-to-GPU mapping and SLA profile advisor
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers asking for recommended reserved throughput and GPU families often get inconsistent guidance: sales gives rough throughput numbers, infra teams ask for GPU-family commitments, and implementation teams need clear scaling policies. The current intake forms and playbooks surface edge cases but do not produce a deterministic mapping that an SRE or solutions engineer can follow without heavy consulting.

Objective: Produce a lightweight, actionable advisor artifact (the 'Capacity Binder') that maps enterprise workload profiles to a recommended reserved throughput band, preferred GPU class families, and a default scaling policy template — all tied to SLA tiers (latency P99, per-customer request RT, and availability). This artifact should be consumable by solutions engineering, sales, and SREs during intake calls and used as an automated suggestion in the intake UI (follow-up project).

Deliverables:
- Capacity Binder doc (Confluence): mapping matrix, examples, and decision tree for ambiguous inputs.
- A short intake questionnaire (6 fields) that yields the recommended profile.
- Ops-ready scaling policy templates (canary / gradual scale / emergency burst) with guardrails.
- Recommendation matrix linking common model types (chat / embeddings / reranking) to GPU families and quantization guidance.
- Hand-off checklist for Dedicated onboarding (what signals to monitor first 72h).

Scope: Non-bug, product-management focused playbook with engineering consultation. Not building UI automation in this ticket; instead produce the artifact and example outputs used by Solutions/AMs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Confluence Capacity Binder published with at least 6 representative customer scenarios and explicit mapping for each.
- Intake questionnaire validated in 3 pilot customer calls and updated once.
- Engineering sign-off on scaling policy templates (ENG owner added to dependencies).
- Clear fallback guidance when preferred GPU family not available (downgrade rules and expected cost/latency delta).
- Metrics and dashboards list (what to observe during first week) included.

Success metrics:
- <20% variance between recommended reserved throughput and observed steady-state 7-day average for pilot customers.
- Onboarding time measured from contract to first stable throughput reduced by 30% for pilots.
- Solutions engineering satisfaction score >= 4/5 in post-pilot survey.

Out-of-scope:
- UI implementation of recommendations (separate ticket).
- Automated enforcement of GPU affinity (requires infra changes).

Notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer to give GPU-family ranges (e.g., A100-40GB, H100-80GB, and an efficient L4-style option) rather than exact SKU to retain flexibility across clouds and on-prem environments.
- For latency-sensitive chat SLAs (P99 < 120ms), recommend smaller batch sizes and H100-class mapping with higher reserved throughput. For batch embedding workloads, recommend larger GPU memory with higher batch parallelism and preferred quantization.
- Aggressive burst tolerance increases cost. We will provide two default templates: Conservative (strict reserved capacity + limited burst) and Elastic (reserved + auto-burst with pre-approved credits).

Follow-ups (future tickets): UI automation for questionnaire, an automated estimator microservice (ENG-...), and telemetry hooks to feed observed load back into recommendation engine.
